newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Warriors taking emotion, pride into final.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Warriors taking emotion, pride into final.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 27 - Popular Auckland prop Hitro Okesene believes emotion and pride will provide the inspiration for the Warriors in Sunday's Optus Cup rugby league reserve grade final against Cronulla in Sydney, NZPA reports.
On the eve of the team's departure for grand finals day at the Sydney Football Stadium, Okesene said the Warriors would not be overawed by the occasion.
"It's a big buzz for everyone at the club, especially for the guys (reserve grade) making this grand final.
"But we've been relaxed this whole week about it. They (Cronulla) might have the experience of having been in the finals before but I think our emotion and pride will get us home.
"For sure I'm confident, and so are the team, that we have it in us to win this one."
He said the Warriors reserves hadn't thought about a shot at the premiership until very late in the season.

"The first time we thought we might be here in the finals weekend was three-quarters of the way through the season. We were starting to look good and we just got better and better. After that it started to become a reality for us."
He said the key to the reserves' season had been the way the side had gelled under Kiwis coach Frank Endacott and the unity they had developed.
"Everyone likes the way Frank coaches and everyone enjoys playing under his relaxed style," Okesene said.
But that relaxed style will disappear on Sunday with the need to start well and maintain momentum, especially up front where the two teams wrestled to a near deadlock in the preliminary rounds.
"It is vital that the forwards get a big roll going, it is really for us to make the yardage up field, get quick play-the-balls going and let the backs finish it off," Okesene said.
"It is going to be a huge tussle up front for us though, because we had a very close game against them in the first round and we only just got home 20-16.
"It went right down to the wire, they were attacking our line right on the last minute or so and we only just kept them out."
The reserves have maintained a low-key approach through the week, trying to keep their routine as normal as possible.
After a rest day today, they will have a light workout at Ericsson Stadium tomorrow before flying out to Sydney in the afternoon.
Teams:

Auckland Warriors: Doc Murray, Paul Staladi, Nigel Vagana, Tony Tatupu, Iva Ropati, Shane Endacott, Aaron Whittaker (captain), Brady Malam, Aaron Lester, Dallas Mead, Tony Tuimavave, Bryan Henare, Logan Swann.
Reserves: Meti Noovao, Paul Rauhihi, Hitro Okesene, Lawrence Tagaloa, Ben Fahey, Gavin Hill.

Cronulla: Ben Sammut, Brett Howland, Russell Richardson, Geoff Bell, Matt Daylight, Kurt Wrigley (captain), Shane Cairns, Stuart Pierce, Paul Fisher, Gavin Jones, Tiaan Strauss, Dione Cope, David Boughton.
Reserves: Andrew Pierce, Adam Dykes, Nick Graham, Wade Forrester, Damian O'Donnell, Matt Clifton, Luke Taper, Jason Buchanan, Bryan Laumatia, Jason Writer, Matt manning, Gavin Dolso.
